event.reason: The global event bus is its own family surface; no per-id operations exist.

health.reason: A single health probe belongs on the root client, not behind a one-method container.

session.reason: The session is the SDK's primary working object: two dozen operations chain on one sessionID (ADR-0019).

message.reason: Message operations are session-scoped and ride the session working object (ADR-0019).

shell.reason: A shell is a live process worked over its id: get, timeout, remove, and the pending output stream (ADR-0019).

integration.reason: The connect and oauth flows are multi-step conversations with one integration; six operations chain on integrationID (ADR-0019).

mcp.reason: The full pinned surface works one server by name - add, remove, connect, disconnect - a lifecycle, not a lookup (ADR-0019).

pty.reason: A pty is a live terminal worked over its id; the pinned surface adds update and connect operations to the trio (ADR-0019). Every public door of the family is hand-written over these raw clients because the WebSocket session and the connect-token handshake need knowledge generation may not import (ADR-0021).

agent.reason: agent.get is the family's only per-id operation; a single lookup takes the id as an argument (ADR-0019).

credential.reason: Update and remove are single-shot admin actions; the id rides as an argument (ADR-0019).

permission.reason: saved.remove is the family's only per-id operation; the pending-request surface lives on sessions (ADR-0019).

provider.reason: provider.get is the family's only per-id operation; a single lookup takes the id as an argument (ADR-0019).

websearch.reason: Query and provider listing carry no per-id operations; a mass-noun container names the domain.

command.reason: The family carries no per-id operations; a flat container holds its calls (ADR-0019).

debug.reason: Diagnostic actions carry no per-id operations; a mass-noun container names the surface (ADR-0019).

experimental.reason: The experimental surface carries no per-id operations; a mass-noun container flags its stability.

generate.reason: The group name is a verb; 'Generates' is not a reviewed .NET name, the mass noun is (ADR-0019).

model.reason: The Models folder and namespace belong to the generated model layer; LanguageModels names the provider model catalog without shadowing either (ADR-0019 flat).

plugin.reason: The family carries no per-id operations; a flat container holds its calls (ADR-0019).

project.reason: The family carries no per-id operations; a flat container holds its calls (ADR-0019).

reference.reason: The family carries no per-id operations; a flat container holds its calls (ADR-0019).

skill.reason: The family carries no per-id operations; a flat container holds its calls (ADR-0019).

vcs.reason: The initialism does not pluralize; the mass-noun container names the domain (ADR-0019).

location.reason: Like health, location resolution is a cross-cutting utility every call can reach directly, not a domain-scoped operation; it belongs on the root client, not behind a one-method container.

server.reason: The server tag is its own domain group, exactly like every other family in this profile; root placement is reserved for the cross-cutting utility probes (health, location), not domain-scoped ones. A flat singular-noun client also leaves room for upstream to grow this group later without a placement change.

workspace.reason: Create and the still-pending destroy are two single-shot admin actions on a workspace id, not a chained working object; the id will ride as an argument once destroy is selected, exactly like credential (ADR-0019).

worktree.reason: The family's full pinned surface (list, create, remove, refresh) all chain on the same projectID, so ADR-0019's full-surface rule gives it a handle now even though only list is selected this batch. The handle is keyed by a project id, not a worktree id, so it is named for what it actually holds: one project's worktree registry.
